title: Jev agent decision layer: from judgment to permission
description: Understand Jev's agent decision layer: typed judgments, runtime permissions, completion evidence, confidence limits and the traps in policy callbacks and shadow mode.

guide_authors.name: Appit Studio
guide_authors.role: Editorial guide; AI-assisted drafting and verification

image.alt: Three responsibility columns: the LLM proposes work, Jev returns bounded judgments, and runtime code checks permissions and executes; observed evidence determines completion or review

connections.step: Inspect the boundary between a typed judgment, policy resolution and an authorized side effect
connections.why: The pinned library separates intended and resolved actions, with inspectable confidence aggregation and shadow handling; its callback order shows why execution must remain outside policy calculation.
connections.limitations: Independent MIT TypeScript library 0.1.0; Node 20+ and TypeSafe access for live inference. Provider calls transmit state/questions and may incur charges even in shadow mode. Policy callback runs before fallback and must be pure. Aggregate confidence can hide a weak required answer. Host owns error handling, permissions and completion verification. Source inspected, not executed; newer upstream revisions exist.

faqs.question: What is a Jev agent decision layer?
faqs.answer: It is a set of bounded semantic judgments around an agent, such as route selection, risk assessment or completion checks. The LLM generates and plans; Jev supplies typed answers; application code enforces permissions and chooses the resulting action.

faqs.question: Can Jev authorize an agent tool call?
faqs.answer: No. A model judgment can inform review, but code must check the exact operation, allowed target, budget and required human approval. Missing evidence, uncertain answers and provider failures must not silently grant permission.

faqs.question: Is a Noul probability the same as confidence?
faqs.answer: No. Noul is the probability that its stated condition is true and has no separate confidence field. Choice and Score include distribution-based confidence. A library may derive another statistic; inspect its formula before using it as a gate.

faqs.question: Can several Jev checks run in one request?
faqs.answer: Yes, when they use the same supplied state and are independent. If one answer determines which evidence to fetch, update the state and make a later request. Put each complete question in its instructions rather than its lookup ID.

faqs.question: Does shadow mode make a Jev harness offline?
faqs.answer: No. The inspected jev-harness version calls TypeSafe before replacing the resolved action with shadow_noop. Use an injected fake client for offline checks, and keep policy callbacks free of side effects.

faqs.question: Does a completion judgment prove the task is finished?
faqs.answer: No. Compare the judgment with observable acceptance evidence, such as test results or a verified artifact. A retry cap can stop a run with work still incomplete; record that state and hand it to review.
